# What upstream has done since each pin was taken

`vendor/README.md` says what we vendor and why we diverge from it. This file says what has happened
*upstream* since, which is the question `script/vendor-verify` deliberately does not ask: it proves
the tree is the published tarball plus our patches, and a proof about the past cannot notice that a
newer past exists.

Regenerated by `script/vendor-watch --write`, which the monthly `vendor watch` workflow runs. It
carries no timestamp on purpose, so an unchanged upstream regenerates a byte-identical file and the
watcher stays silent; a diff here means upstream moved.

**This file reports. It decides nothing.** A newer version is not automatically a better one, and
the pins in this directory were taken deliberately. What to do about a gap is in
`vendor/README.md`'s "Bumping a pin" section.

## redoxfs

Pinned at upstream git commit `db847d87c680`, which no release carries; its manifest says **0.9.1**.

**Releases: current.** 0.9.1 is still the newest published version that is neither yanked nor a prerelease.

**Upstream git: 3 non-merge commits** since the pinned sha (plus 1 merge commits, dropped), head `5ba45a688737`.

Full comparison: https://gitlab.redox-os.org/redox-os/redoxfs/-/compare/db847d87c68052618d1427537c7277293a626a18...5ba45a6887374ab425326656a276bb3b62eba7dc

- 2026-10-31 `01140853` Avoid leaking a handle for each bound unix sockets
- 2026-10-31 `5251b59b` Switch to the 2024 edition
- 2026-10-31 `1134c94f` Directly provide socket entrypoint fd to the user

**Upstream has edited files our divergence patch also touches**, so a bump is likely to conflict there:
